55040.subject: Government
55040.explanation: Legal sovereignty shouldn't be unquestionable because in a democratic system, the powers of the legislature should be subject to necessary executive and judicial review respectively for the sake of checks and balance and accountability.

55041.subject: Government
55041.question_text: That type of sovereignty that thrives on legitimacy is__________
55041.explanation: Sovereignty that thrives on legitimacy is often referred to as popular sovereignty or political sovereignty, which means that the authority of the government is derived from the people's consent. This aligns with the idea of sovereignty being within the people's mandate, as legitimacy is granted through democratic processes such as elections, referenda, and public support.

options.text: vested on any form of government

55043.subject: Government
55043.question_text: The right of a citizen to seek redress means the right to________
55043.explanation: Seek an appeal under another judgement is the best answer because,  ''the right to seek redress'' is a fundamental element of rule of law. It means that aggrieved parties should be afforded the opportunity to have their cases re-examined especially by a court of higher authority.

options.text: seek an appeal under another judgement

55045.subject: Government
55045.question_text: An order compelling a lower court or public corporation to perform in accordance with legitimacy is called_________
55045.explanation: Writ (i.e Order) of Mandamus is usually issued to mandate a public authority to perform its statutory or the functions tied to its establishment. On the alternative, the great writ means the habeas corpus writ issued to order the release of a body or person unlawfully detained or imprisoned to stand judgement

55046.subject: Government
55046.question_text: A form of government which has its slogan to be 'ruling of the best' is__________
55046.explanation: Aristocracy being a rule by the Noble is believed to be a ruling of the best class of persons. Timocracy on the other hand, is believed by Aristotle to be a government strictly by property-owners with emphasis on honour and proprietary interest holdings.

55049.subject: Government
55049.explanation:
Deconcentration involves the passing down of selected administrative functions to lower levels or units within government agencies or departments with the centre remaining in control

Like the series of political office arrangements and portfolios in the Hausa/Fulani Empire i.e the Galadima, Waziri and the rest, deconcentration of power is obtainable unlike in devolution which Options B and D implicitly cover. Option A refers to the Decentralization of powers.

options.text: sharing of powers among tiers of government
creation of semi autonomous units to govern other parts of a state
process of setting strategies or policies for the subsidiary territories in the state by putting recognized personnel in place
act of delegating powers and authority to component units that exist in a state

55050.subject: Government
55050.question_text: The concept of the independence of the judiciary means that________
55050.explanation: Strictly speaking, independence of the judiciary isn't restricted to the idea of non-interference by the legislature or executive or either of agencies on judicial decision making but particularly ensuring that all the gateways to the activities that may put the judiciary in a vulnerable state to the other arms of government must be shut down.

options.text: The judiciary must not attempt to meddle into legislative and executive affairs
The powers of the courts can not be subjected of executive re-assessment
The sanctity of the office of the Judges and Justices must be preserved without prejudice
All means of legislative or executive influence on judicial decision making must be disabled

55051.subject: Government
55051.explanation: Political parties act as a means through which various interests and concerns of the people are represented and advocated for within the political system. They aggregate diverse viewpoints and channel them into actionable policies, ensuring that the voices of different groups are heard in governance.

options.text: A platform upon which the rights and liberties of the people can be attained
The group aggregating the interest of all in the state
A platform for rebelling against military rule

55052.subject: Government
55052.question_text: A party can be said to have national outlook if________
55052.explanation: Unlike the ethnic based philosophy, nature or outlook of the Action Group, Northern Peoples Congress in the First Republic, a multi-ethnic and all embracing political party is that with a Nation wide outlook

options.text: it is ethnic based but has branches all over the state
its membership cut across ethnic boundaries
it is registered by the electoral commission as a national party
it is headed by individuals who are famous within and without the country

55054.subject: Government
55054.question_text: Argumentation, negotiation and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begins at the_______
55054.explanation: At the second stage or reading of a bill, the debate on the subject matter of concern of the bill begins, this process becomes heightened at the Third Stage and particularly at the Committee Stage.

55056.subject: Government
55056.explanation: vote of no confidence; a vote showing that a majority does not support the policy of a leader or governing body.

options.text: the same as impeachment in a presidential system
the ability of the head of state to dissolve the parliament when collective responsibility fails to hold
the act of showing disapproval to the prime minister having breached the collective responsibility doctrine
the disapproval with dismissal in effect, the ministers and its head

55059.subject: Government
55059.explanation: A cabinet reshuffle takes place when dissolution is held. In parliamentary systems, a cabinet reshuffle may occur when there is a general election and the government is dissolved, leading to a need for reorganizing the cabinet with new ministers or changing existing ones. The membership of the Cabinet will be substituted or reshuffled, especially when there is the dissolution of the cabinet in its entirety in a Parliamentary/ Westminster system.

options.text: only when a motion of no confidence is passed
when prorogation and collective responsibility have their way
when the shadow cabinet fails in its effectiveness

55060.subject: Government
55060.explanation: The sum total of all activities exerted by the majority with enthusiasm actively involving in all aspects of their political sphere is the best answer not only because is the all-encompassing answer but also because popular political participation is the aggregation of all efforts of the citizens partaking deliberately and consciously in their governance affairs.

options.text: having majority of the people partaking in politics
having a good number of voters in the electoral process
the aggregate efforts of more than half of the citizens to partake in public debate and politics
the sum total of all activities exerted by the majority with enthusiasm actively involving in all aspects of their political sphere

55063.subject: Government
55063.question_text: The area from which one or more members or representatives are elected in public offices is called the electoral ........
55063.explanation: Constituency is the definition for the political area from which an individual is elected into a representative office.

55065.subject: Government
55065.explanation: Citizenship by naturalization provides the medium for non-citizens who have satisfied or fulfilled the requirements of good citizenship according to a State Law, to become Citizens.

options.text: is the same as citizenship by marriage and registeration
refers to the process of attaining citizenship through honorary means
is the act of a non-citizen having satisfied the constitutional criteria becoming a legal member of a state
is the medium by which an alien through the judiciary receives certification and attains citizenship by birth

55066.subject: Government
55066.question_text: The last measure used by the pressure groups issuing a condition to be satisfied within a stipulated time is called_______
55066.explanation: Pressure groups commonly issued deadlines(ultimatum) for the government to fulfill their requests and queries before embarking on strike action.

55068.subject: Government
55068.question_text: Generally, a political party with only manifestoes without fulfilment is a/an _____
55068.explanation: Elitist is often used as a critique label, to describe a political party definitive of social class and rankings of top profiled politicians without much agenda for social justice. Elitist parties are often seen as focusing more on presenting themselves as representatives of a particular elite or ideology rather than actively implementing their policies or fulfilling their promises.

55071.subject: Government
55071.question_text: A form of government organized by a council of military officers is called______
55071.explanation: A stratocracy is a form of government headed by military chiefs.

55072.subject: Government
55072.question_text: The non-stratified society in the pre-colonial era was that of the ........ where decisions were made________
55072.explanation: The Igbo precolonial was seen as ''headless'' and decisions were made based on popular consultations and acceptability.

55073.subject: Government
55073.question_text: The Hausa/Fulani Empire as a result of its heterogeneous population adopted_________
55073.explanation: The hausa/fulani empire for geo-political reasons apportioned different portfolios of authorities for serve the multiplicity of functions and administrative interests. The offices of Sarkin fada, as head of palace workers, Waziri as prime minister among others are pointers in this regard.

options.text: A unitary system where full concentration of power prevailed
A federal structure where powers were decentralized although autocratic
A quasi federal structure with devolution
A partial federal set up with deconcentration

55076.subject: Government
55076.question_text: Twelve States creation is a known achievement of the ... regime
55076.explanation: Yakubu Gowon created 12 states for Nigeria in 1967.

55077.subject: Government
55077.question_text: The basis of the Nigerian foreign policy thrust particularly during the Independence Constitution era was ... in nature
55077.explanation: Afrocentrism is the term used to describe the nature and interests of the Nigerian foreign policy targets withy preference for African neighboring States.

55078.subject: Government
55078.question_text: The Brussel conference in 1889/90 was based on______
55078.explanation: The Brussel Conference unlike the Berlin Conference was targeted at the reconsideration of the unjust virtues and vices occasioned by colonialism, thereby specifically seeking to eradicate slave trade and related activities.

options.text: putting an end to slave trade
furthering the decision on colonialism as previously discussed in the Berlin conference
deciding on how to penetrate Africa for economic adventurism

55080.subject: Government
55080.question_text: According to Lewis Samuel, '________ is identified with pure conquest and unequivocal exploitation...'
55080.explanation: The ideology of regressive imperialism is pure economic advantage and enrichment of the imperialists devoid of any ethical consideration.

55082.subject: Government
55082.question_text: One of the major defects of the Nigerian council which necessitated its replacement was that....
55082.explanation: The unrepresentative nature and figurehead stance of the Nigerian Council's membership is a stand-alone reason for the flaw of the platform. Most members were Whites who didn't understand the interests of the people they seek to govern.

options.text: the meetings of the council were poorly attended
the council could only make law for the southern protectorate
the executive council was powerful than it

55084.subject: Government
55084.question_text: An important provision of the 1946 constitution was that it ........
55084.explanation: The Authur Richard Constitution of 1946 set the foundational road map for a full fledged federalism for Nigeria starting essentially with the Lyttleton's 1954 Constitution, and built upon thereafter.

options.text: introduced official majority in the legislative council for the 1st time
for the 1st time, introduced the office of the head of government at the regional level

55086.subject: Government
55086.explanation: The All-Nigerian Constitutional Conference of 1950, held in Ibadan, was a significant event in Nigeria’s constitutional development. Delegates from different regions of Nigeria met to discuss the future political structure of the country. One of the key resolutions of the conference was the adoption of a quasi-federal system, which meant that Nigeria would move towards a federal system of government but with some centralized features. This decision later influenced the Macpherson Constitution of 1951, which introduced regional legislatures and a degree of autonomy for the three regions (Northern, Western, and Eastern regions).

options.text: all official members of the legislative council participated
it was resolved that the Nigerians federation be organized on ethnic basis
it was concluded that a quasi-federal structure should be developed for colonial Nigeria
all unofficial members of the legislative council participated

55088.subject: Government
55088.question_text: Implementations of the target programmes of the government is the primary duty of the _____ a part of the _____
55088.explanation: The Civil Service is an integral branch of the public service which primarily functions to implement the policies of the government.

55089.subject: Government
55089.question_text: The most recent target plans and agenda of the United Nations are known as the______
55089.explanation: The 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are the most recent aspirational global agenda for the sake of environmental sustainability, strong governance institutions and partnerships among related others.

55091.subject: Government
55091.question_text: The federal judge under the 1963 constitution could be removed by the______
55091.explanation: 2/3 majority support or vote of the National Assembly members was enough under the 1963 Constitution to remove a federal judge.

55093.subject: Government
55093.question_text: Under the 1999 constitution, the Chief Law Officer and the Supreme Court Judge respectively are the_______
55093.explanation: The Attorney General of the Federation is the same as the Minister of Justice while the judge at the Supreme Court level is the Chief Justice.

options.text: Chief Registrar of the Supreme Court, Chief Justice

55094.subject: Government
55094.question_text: Which of the following was not responsible for the coalition between A. G and N. C. N. C.?
55094.explanation: All the following options facilitated the coalition of the action Group and the National Council of the Nigerian Citizens except the The Kano Riot of 1953

options.text: Awolowo's faction seeking to get N. P. C. out of power as opposed to Akintola's option
contest for the federal election of 1964
Akintola's faction which broke out of A. G. to form UPP

55096.subject: Government
55096.question_text: In the 4th republic, the political parties were______
55096.explanation:
In the 4th Republic of Nigeria, which began in 1999, the main political parties were:

  • PDP (Peoples Democratic Party)

  • APP (All Peoples Party)

  • AD (Alliance for Democracy)

These parties were the dominant players in the political landscape during the early years of the 4th Republic.

55097.subject: Government
55097.question_text: The Economic and Financials Crime Commission (EFCC) scope and nature of duty may not extend to_______
55097.explanation: The EFCC as it is, is an executive body that must discharge its functions strictly in line with the reasons for its establishment. None of those functions extend to exercising judicial powers by punishing and conducting trials for suspects, which the strict duty of the court.

options.text: arresting suspects of cyber crime and online fraud
arresting the giver and the taker in a corruption case
conducting trials and punishing persons involved in corruption matters
investigating cases of substance and drug abuse intersecting with money laundering

55100.subject: Government
55100.question_text: The Green Revolution programme was the effected manifesto of the ........ in 1979
55100.explanation: The National Party of Nigeria (NPN) is popularly known for its Green Revolution agricultural project in the late 1979s.

55101.subject: Government
55101.question_text: Nigeria's federalism is often considered a flaw along the standard test of the Classical federalism ideology labelled along with_______
55101.explanation: Kenneth Clinton Wheare is noted to having postulated that the fundamental, negotiable element of federalism is voluntary submission of rights by the component units in a federal set up.

55102.subject: Government
55102.question_text: The most representative organ of the united nations is the_______
55102.explanation: General Assembly. The UN General Assembly comprises the Heads of State and Government of all the State Parties in the UN body.

55104.subject: Government
55104.question_text: Executive Council of the African Union makes decision by_______
55104.explanation: The Council of Ministers of the State Parties of the AU, the Executive Council makes decision primarily by consensus or by 2/3 majority support.

options.text: the veto of the General Secretariat

55105.subject: Government
55105.question_text: Amendment of the U. N. O. charter is the duty of the ........
55105.explanation: The UN General Assembly has the duty of amending relevant provisions of the UN Charter.

55106.subject: Government
55106.question_text: The fact that the office of the Chairman is rotational in ECOWAS makes it a perfect example of a/an ........
55106.explanation: A Collegiate is used to describe a rotational system of governance within a specific circle of qualified practitioners or representatives.

55276.subject: Government
55276.question_text: The newspaper established by Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe to project the interest of nationalists was__________
55276.explanation: The West African Pilot was the newspaper of Dr Azikiwe which served as a medium for propagating nationalist ideas and solidarity movements towards self-realization.

55278.subject: Government
55278.question_text: The delineation of electoral constituencies for reasons of political advantage is termed___________
55278.explanation: Gerrymandering is the process of creating political constituencies in order to favour the electoral scores of a political party.

55280.subject: Government
55280.question_text: A predominant feature of the Precolonial governance system was that_________
55280.explanation: Throughout the precolonial era in Nigeria, the native laws of the people governed them. They were largely unwritten and enforced by distinct units set in place for those purposes.

options.text: the British Indirect rule system penetrated it largely
the governance structures were largely undefined

55281.subject: Government
55281.question_text: In most recent times, a seemingly workable solution to the Nigerian federal question is that of_______
55281.explanation: Although Options A, B and C are recurring options for the Nigerian federalism, the clarion call for restructuring is louder than ever before.

55283.subject: Government
55283.question_text: The concept of delegated legislation is often criticised for all but one of the following reasons?
55283.explanation: Delegated Legislation is supported largely because certain specialist idea is needed for the purpose of rule making on areas upon which the legislature may not have sufficient knowledge and skill in. Example, the INEC is empowered to make election guidelines and regulations aside the Electoral Act and in furtherance of its duties.

options.text: it may lead to abuse of the powers
for reasons of sheer ignorance on legislative substance and procedure
for reasons of expertise rule making on specific subject matters
it is a clear violation of the separation of powers concept

55287.subject: Government
55287.question_text: ____ is noted for having said "man by nature is a political animal"
55287.explanation: According to Aristotle, every human interaction intersects with political determinations and interests.

55289.subject: Government
55289.explanation: A public authority is said to have ultra vires when it has acted beyond the boundaries of its duties as provided for in its enabling law or as prescribed by the Executive.

options.text: the exercise of supervisory functions by the judiciary
a situation where a public authority dutifully performs its functions
a situation where a public authority acts beyond the scope of its duties
the act of exercising administrative competence over a matter

55291.subject: Government
55291.question_text: Class stratification is a peculiar feature of___________
55291.explanation: In a capitalist system, there is a clear differentiation gap between the ruling class and the ruled or the proletarates.

55292.subject: Government
55292.question_text: One of the following reasons is unlikely to necessitate the emergence of a federal system?
55292.explanation: Other options are necessary reasons for the adoption of a federal system except for sake of defining or strengthening the political sovereignty which invariably belongs to the citizens.

55296.subject: Government
55296.question_text: Lobbying is often a strategy adopted by________
55296.explanation: Pressure groups often adopt lobbying as a negotiation mechanism with critical governement stakeholders and or legislators so that significant policies and laws giving effect to their interests are implemented.

55298.subject: Government
55298.question_text: A political party often with a radical viewpoint and perspective to sensitive state affairs matters is often labelled as a ___party
55298.explanation: A liberal political party often seeks to argue for change and transformation of the present state of things in a state including those matters of relative social and economic importance.

55300.subject: Government
55300.question_text: Opinion sampling may be necessary for the following reasons except________
55300.explanation: To inspire public reasoning on population census is the best answer, as it is the least reason why opinion sampling mechanisms, by way of online survey or through opinion polls are organised.

options.text: for aggregating popular thinking and standpoint on a subject matter
to evaluate the political strength of a political party
to inspire public reasoning on population census

55302.subject: Government
55302.question_text: The defining processes for the formation of a people's political behaviour is___________
55302.explanation: Political socialisation refers to the series of learning processes and experiences which serve to sharpen the orientation and perspective of the people to their democratic affairs.

55304.subject: Government
55304.question_text: The ____ Reform is influential to the inception of Local Government in Nigeria
55304.explanation: The Murtala/Obasanjo 1976 Reform necessitated the discovery of the essence of a local government council and establishment.

55307.subject: Government
55307.question_text: Colonialist arrival in Nigeria is traceable particularly to the_____
55307.explanation: It must be stated with emphatic clarity that the annexation of Lagos as a 'Colony' in 1861 is significant to the effectuation of colonialism in Nigeria. All the other factors of economic advantage and the spread of christianity are complementary and implied reasons.

options.text: introduction of the indirect rule policy

55308.subject: Government
55308.explanation: The indigénat policy was introduced by the French colonies in various forms and degrees of severity to control and exploit the French colonial population and subject them to arbitrary punishments, forced labour and a separate court system. It was an obnoxious policy that gave French officials the right to arbitrarily arrest and imprison any African for about two yeas without trial.

55310.subject: Government
55310.question_text: The solidarity for self-governance system and liberty of Africans demonstrated by Africans and Non-Africans in diaspora is termed__________
55310.explanation: Pan-Africanism is the ideology upheld by a wide majority of the advocates for the independence of African States during the colonialism era and beyond.

55312.subject: Government
55312.question_text: Acceleration of the independence movements in the British West African Colonies was essentially because of the________
55312.explanation: The tolerance posture for the development of political parties and interest groups in the British West African Colonies spurred the pace of the drive for their autonomy.

options.text: posture of the British Governor Generals
tolerance for political participation and demonstration through political parties
speedy grant of independence in the French Colonies

55313.subject: Government
55313.question_text: The cultural organisation which metamorphosed into the Northern People's Congress (NPC) was__________
55313.explanation: The Northern People's Congress was an offshoot of the Jamiyyar Mutanen Arewa.

55314.subject: Government
55314.question_text: The legitimate claims and entitlements available by reasons of birth and residence and/or certification, to a community of people may be abscribed as their___________
55314.explanation: Citizenship rights are the legal privileges and opportunities available to the citizens of a State. Examples, only citizens are eligible to contest elections and own properties in Nigeria. Fundamental rights and civil liberties are an aggregation of their individual and collective entitlements by reasons of being human.

55317.subject: Government
55317.question_text: A moral or legal conviction for the observance of the constitution may be described as________
55317.explanation: Constitutionalism is the term used to describe compliance with the provisions of the constitution.

55318.subject: Government
55318.question_text: The primary essence of a public corporation is__________
55318.explanation: The primary essence of a public corporation is public utility. Public corporations are established primarily to provide services or utilities to the public. Although they generate profit, this is not their primary aim.

options.text: for the formulation of government policies
for the resolution of administrative disputes

55320.subject: Government
55320.question_text: The principle that determines the pattern of interaction of a country in international politics is known as____________
55320.explanation: The foreign policy thrust of a state defines its delibrate and strategic plan of actions in interaction with other states.

55321.subject: Government
55321.question_text: The arm of government responsible for the approval of war is the_____
55321.explanation: While declaration of war is the duty of the executive, the legislature approves or disapproves of it as embarking on war means and requires additional expenditure and budget scrutiny.

55323.subject: Government
55323.question_text: The West African Students' Union (WASU) was formed in____________
55323.explanation: WASU was formed by Chief Ladipo Solanke among others in 1925.

55324.subject: Government
55324.question_text: The Chick's commission was set up to look into the issue of revenue allocation in___________
55324.explanation: As part of the Commissions set up for the review of the Nigerian federalism challenges, the Chick's commission was set up in 1953.

55325.subject: Government
55325.question_text: The head of the districts in the Hausa/Fulani Empire were the_________
55325.explanation: The Hakimi was the titled administrative officers in charge of the districts in the heterogeneous Hausa/Fulani Empire.

55326.subject: Government
55326.question_text: Under the 1979 constitution of Nigeria, each State was allowed to elect________
55326.explanation: Unlike the position under the present 1999 Constitution as amended, each state was permitted to elect 5 senators into the House of Representatives.

options.text: from two to five senators depending on the population
as many senators as the state could finance.

55328.subject: Government
55328.question_text: The Armed Forces Ruling Council (AFRC) is attributable to the ____ regime
55328.explanation: Unlike the Supreme Military Council of the Muhammadu Buhari's military regime, the AFRC is attributtable to the Babangida's regime.

55329.subject: Government
55329.question_text: The dwindling and market falls in oil prices are prime indicators for Nigeria politico-economic consideration for________
55329.explanation: In most recent times, the prevalent politico-economic discussions in Nigeria has been on the need for economic diversification for reasons of economic boom and social transformation.

options.text: the adoption of the United Nations' Vision 2030

55330.subject: Government
55330.question_text: Nigeria's top contribution to Africa's agenda of decolonisation and anti-racism was mostly enhanced with the formation of the_________
55330.explanation: In the wake of the call for the decolonisation of Africa, Nigeria actively contributed to the formation of the OAU for a solidarity movement in that direction.

options.text: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)

55332.subject: Government
55332.question_text: One of the following political parties produced Nigeria's first Prime Minister_______
55332.explanation: NPC was the party of Tafawa Balewa, Nigeria's first prime minister.

55334.subject: Government
55334.question_text: The National Assembly in the second republic was made up of the________
55334.explanation: The Chambers of the National Assembly since 1979 are the House of Representatives and the Senate respectively. The National Assembly was bicameral, consisting of these two chambers. The Senate was the upper chamber, while the House of Representatives was the lower chamber.

options.text: House of Chiefs and the Senate
Lower House and the House of Representatives
Senate and the House of Lords

55336.subject: Government
55336.question_text: The All Progressives Congress (APC) is the result of a coalition of the following parties except the___________
55336.explanation: APC is the result of the merger of the parties in options A, B, and D including a faction of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA).

55337.subject: Government
55337.question_text: The process by which electorates remove elected official is called_________
55337.explanation: The power of impeachment belongs to the legislature to check the Executive act of gross misconduct while Re-call is exercisable within the reach of the electorates. This procedure allows voters to remove and replace a public official before the end of their term of office. It is a form of direct democracy that provides a way for the electorate to ensure accountability of elected officials.

55340.subject: Government
55340.question_text: The Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) is an organ of the_________
55340.explanation: ECOSOC is an organ of the UN basically concerned with matters of economic and socio-cultural importance to the global community.

55342.subject: Government
55342.question_text: Nigeria joined the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) in__________
55342.explanation: Nigeria joined OPEC in 1971 during Yakubu Gowon's military regime.

55345.subject: Government
55345.question_text: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has its headquarters in__________
55345.explanation: The ICC sits at the Hagues, Netherlands. The ICC is an intergovernmental organisation and international tribunal that prosecutes individuals for crimes of genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and the crime of aggression. The Hague is known as the city of peace and justice and it houses several international legal institutions, including the ICC.

55348.subject: Government
55348.question_text: The current Secretary-General of the United Nations is_________
55348.explanation: As of 2019, Antonio Guterres, a Portuguese diplomat was the ninth serving Secretary-General of the United Nations. He assumed office on January 1, 2017, succeeding Ban Ki-moon. Antonio Guterres is a Portuguese politician and diplomat who previously served as the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees from 2005 to 2015. His extensive experience in international relations and commitment to addressing global challenges have been central to his role as the Secretary-General.
